title: Hunger within, shame on the face
literal_meaning: Hunger in the belly, shame on the face.
meaning_odia: ପେଟ ଭୋକିଲା, ଅଥଚ ମୁହଁରେ ଲାଜ। ଦରକାର ଥିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ତାହା କହିବାକୁ ବା ମାଗିବାକୁ ସଙ୍କୋଚ ଲାଗିବା—ଏହା ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠ। ଲାଜ କାହିଁକି ଲାଗୁଛି ବା କାହା ପାଖରେ ଲାଗୁଛି, ପଙ୍କ୍ତିରେ କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
explanation: A bodily need is set beside an emotion that can keep it unspoken. Our editorial reading is of someone who is hungry but too embarrassed to ask. More broadly, the compact contrast can describe a genuine need concealed by shyness, without saying why the person feels that way.
usage_example: Original imagined example: A guest has not eaten but keeps quiet when food is offered. A friend gently recalls the line about hunger in the belly and shame on the face, making room for an honest answer.
cultural_context: The line needs only two locations: the belly holds the need, while the face displays embarrassment. This economy gives the saying its force without naming a household rule or particular occasion.
